{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.21","title":"radio.py: polling RX success re-notifies and inflates NodeMetrics","description":"## Problem

`_get_rx_result_internal` documents an idempotent polling path: "idempotent record_reception + node.record_rx + rx_success log + on_rx_success observer" and "single log/notify per test oracle."

Only `Metrics.record_reception` is actually idempotent (keyed on `(rx_node_id, tx_id)`). After that call, every subsequent poll during the same airtime still:

1. Calls `node.metrics.record_rx()` — `NodeMetrics.record_rx` always does `rx_count += 1` / `rx_bytes += len(payload)` with no delivery key (`python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py` ~L75-88).
2. Emits `rx_success` via `_debug_log`.
3. Calls `_observers.notify("on_rx_success", ...)`.

The collision arm already gates log+notify on `record_collision(...)` returning True. The success arm has no equivalent gate.

The simulator polls `get_rx_result` on a ~1 ms interval while a node waits (`metrics.py` module docstring). `test_metrics.py` `test_reception_not_double_counted_on_poll` only asserts `sim.metrics.receptions == 1`. `test_radio.py` never re-polls a successful `get_rx_result`, so NodeMetrics inflation and observer duplication are untested.

Callback `deliver_pending_packets` is not affected (it leaves RX_WAIT before a second poll). Polling / HIL loops that call `get_rx_result` repeatedly during airtime are.

## Why this is robustness

A long-running poll loop (WebSocket viz, TUI, BARRIER_SYNC RX wait, tests that poll until hit) floods observers and inflates per-node `rx_count`/`rx_bytes`/`unique_peers` while global `Metrics.receptions` stays honest. Duty-cycle and delivery dashboards that mix the two disagree. Collision handling already fail-closes on first observation; success does not.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_get_rx_result_internal` success path ~L591-640; docstring claims idempotent node.record_rx + notify)
- `python/tests/sim/test_radio.py` (no re-poll of successful RX)
- `python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py` (`NodeMetrics.record_rx` not keyed; `Metrics.record_reception` is)
